summary: Gone first Faunce tower, replaced by the 1935 CCC tower; the county list says only a concrete foundation piece remains. Sources disagree on the distance.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 survey note puts the new tower about a mile north of the old one; the tourism guide puts the old tower three miles south. The listed coordinates of the two sites are about three miles apart. Both sources place the old tower south of the current one, so only the distance is in dispute. The story reports both figures.

notes_for_editor: The link between the directory's Faunce – first (48.55044, -94.95354) and the county list's first Faunce Fire Tower (48.5505, -94.9533) rests on the matching coordinates and the 'first' name; the county text places that tower south of the extant site. No build date for the first tower appears in any source read, so the story gives none. The distance disagreement (about a mile per the 1934 note, three miles per the guide and per the coordinates) is reported in the story. The current Faunce record (us-mn-faunce) repeats the three-mile figure and does not mention the 1934 note; its editor may want to add it. The county list also gives an overall height of about 150 feet for the 1935 tower in a 1966 survey note, which conflicts with its 100-foot design; that is outside this record and was not checked. Confidence is medium.
